change.description: Span Buffer Multiprocess Enhancement with Health Monitoring
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is false for spawned processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: The processes are created with `mp_context.Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` and `multiprocessing.Process` (`context.Process`) are sibling subclasses of `BaseProcess`. `isinstance(spawn_proc, multiprocessing.Process)` is therefore False. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now a hung ('hang' cause) process is never killed, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second flusher on the same shards while the first is still running. The same check at line 346 means `join` never terminates the processes. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or `mp_context.Process` instead, or call `kill()` unless the process is a `threading.Thread`.

findings.title: join leaves later processes alive once the deadline passes
findings.body: When the deadline expires, the loop `break`s before reaching the remaining processes. Those processes are neither waited on nor terminated, though `stopped` is set. Terminate the remaining processes even after the timeout. This matters more because the `terminate` branch is already skipped for spawned processes (see the isinstance finding).

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test patches time.sleep
findings.body: `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` replaces `time.sleep` globally. The added `time.sleep(0.1)` therefore does nothing, so the 'give flusher threads time' comment is false and the test can still race. Wait on a condition instead, for example poll until `messages` is non-empty with a bounded loop. Also, `test_flusher_processes_limit` never submits messages, so it only checks the shard-to-process mapping.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: `wait_produce` is tagged `shards`, while the neighbouring metrics use `shard`. Both carry the same comma-joined value. Dashboards will split on the two names, so use one.

findings.title: Memory info is queried once per buffer
findings.body: Every `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, which covers the whole cluster (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:375). Looping over N buffers on every `submit` repeats the same query N times and sums identical values into `used` and `available`. The ratio is roughly unchanged, but the cost grows with N. Query one buffer only.

contracts.equivalent_path: Old `_ensure_process_alive` called self.process.kill() unconditionally, then recreated the process
contracts.before_after: The new code kills only if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is False for SpawnProcess, so the hung process is left running and a duplicate is started
contracts.visible_effect: Duplicate flushers on the same shards after a hang; possible double production of segments

contracts.equivalent_path: Old join waited on a single process until the deadline
contracts.before_after: Now it loops over all processes against one shared deadline, which is a correct overall bound, but processes after the deadline are not terminated
contracts.visible_effect: Shutdown stays bounded by the timeout; stragglers are left behind
contracts.failure_mode: Daemon processes are left running until the parent exits

summary: The multi-process flusher has one real bug. The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check is False for spawned processes, so hung flushers are never killed on restart and `join` never terminates them. That can leave duplicate flushers running on the same shards. There are also smaller issues: `join` skips processes after the deadline, the new test's `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is patched, one metric tag is spelled `shards` instead of `shard`, and memory info is queried once per buffer. I only read the code and ran nothing.
